items.title: SQLite foreign_keys pragma never enabled — declared cascade FKs not actually enforced
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 by the BUG-33 schema brief. Original claim: src/backend/db/index.ts has no `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` anywhere, and plain SQLite disables FK enforcement by default per-connection — concluded that declared cascades were decorative only. CORRECTED 2026-07-20, same session: the BUG-32 backend brief independently hit this exact question (a real production 500 on deleting a place with items still referencing it — only possible if the FK constraint IS being enforced) and empirically verified via an isolated @libsql/client script that FK enforcement is ON by default with this driver, no explicit pragma needed. COO independently reproduced the same test directly (DELETE against a referenced parent row failed with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY) and confirms this. The original claim was a correct fact about the plain SQLite C library that doesn't hold for @libsql/client specifically — this codebase's actual driver. No orphaned-row risk exists; closing as not-a-bug. The real bug this surfaced (items.trip_place_id has no onDelete behavior specified, so deleting a place with items throws a 500 instead of cascading or reassigning) was fixed independently in PR #166 (BUG-32) via reassign-to-null rather than cascade-delete, to preserve logged items.

items.title: items.carriedFromItemId has no onDelete FK behavior — trip deletion 500s if a carried-forward item still references it
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 by the WP-03/WP-04 Frontend brief (PR #208) while writing E2E coverage for the carried-forward tag — pre-existing defect, not introduced by that PR. Symptom: DELETE /api/trips/:id 500s if any of the trip's items was ever used as a carry-forward source (items.carried_from_item_id) for an item in ANY other trip, including trips since modified/locked/unlocked (the reference persists independent of trip status). Root cause: carriedFromItemId is a self-referencing FK (.references(() => items.id)) with no .onDelete(...) clause — SQLite/@libsql FK enforcement (confirmed ON by default, see BUG-38) defaults to RESTRICT. ARCHITECT RULING 2026-07-21 (ADL-36, jobs/architect/tech/20260307-architecture-decisions-log.md, GitHub issue #209, PR #212 merged): onDelete: 'set null' CONFIRMED (High confidence) — cascade rejected (would destroy an independent item on another trip), restrict is the bug. Verified safe against every current consumer: UpdateItemSchema does not expose the carry-forward fields (PATCH can't re-validate the coupling), the frontend tag reads the is_carried_forward boolean not the FK, no read path assumes carried_from_item_id non-null, and the partial index is already WHERE ... IS NOT NULL — NO backend/frontend change needed. The resulting is_carried_forward=1 / carried_from_item_id=NULL state is INTENTIONAL (create-time coupling per ADL-13 only; is_carried_forward is the permanent fact, the FK is a nullable provenance pointer). FK audit: BUG-39 is ISOLATED — every other no-onDelete FK references soft-deleted admin lists (never hard-deleted) or non-deletable geo/seed tables; items.tripPlaceId's omission is BUG-32's deliberate app-level reassign. No follow-up bug entry. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-21 (PR #214, merged, all 9 CI checks green): carriedFromItemId FK now onDelete: 'set null' in schema.ts; migration 0011_majestic_nehzno.sql generated via db:generate/db:migrate (never db:push) — table-recreation SQL eyeballed, self-FK ON DELETE SET NULL / partial index idx_items_carried / all 3 chk_items_* CHECK constraints / existing row data all confirmed intact. schema.ts doc comment updated recording the intentional post-deletion state. Regression test added (trips.delete.test.ts) asserting DELETE /api/trips/:id returns 204 (was 500) with the derived item surviving, carried_from_item_id nulled, is_carried_forward unchanged — self-verified against a reverted fix to confirm it's a real regression guard. Deleting an individual source item directly was confirmed to hit the same constraint, also fixed by this change. GitHub issue #209 (closed via PR #214). Full discovery write-up: jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260721-FRONTEND-wp03wp04-park.txt.

(1) BUG-33 schema-half agent: bare `git stash`/`git stash pop` collided with a concurrent agent's stash — refs/stash is a single ref shared across all linked worktrees, unlike HEAD/branch/index/working-directory which isolation:"worktree" does cover. (2) Same BUG-33 schema-half agent separately ran initial investigation commands against /workspace (shared COO tree) before noticing it hadn't cd'd into its assigned worktree — caught before any lasting changes (reads + one throwaway test file, since deleted). Fix: CLAUDE.md's Agent dispatch isolation section extended with two new mandatory rules — no bare git stash/stash pop (use git diff to a scratch file instead), and every worktree dispatch must confirm its working directory matches the assigned worktree path as its first action. No GitHub issue raised — direct COO-session process fix, no code/app impact.

items.title: Agent read-only diagnostic access to Railway, Turso, Clerk (ADL-33)
items.notes: Operational tooling, no BRD ID (ADL-33 §8). Triggered 2026-07-21 by manual log-relay pain during a live Railway deploy debug session. Architect ADL-33: Turso GRANT (clean, DB-scoped read-only tokens); Railway GRANT WITH CAVEAT (no read-only token scope exists); Clerk DO NOT GRANT. PO confirmed both. IMPLEMENTED (PR #181, merged): Turso + Railway hosts added to init-firewall.sh; .env.agent-diagnostics (gitignored) with both Turso tokens (verified via JWT claim inspection — distinct per-database `rid`, not account/group-scoped, after an initial false start with a mistakenly-pasted account-level token, flagged for revocation, never used) and both Railway tokens (one per environment — PO provided one for each rather than prod-only; verified via GraphQL auth — distinct environmentId per token confirms real per-environment scoping). scripts/agent-diagnostics/turso-query.mjs and railway-query.sh (read-only query runners) + runbook. Railway's official CLI does not work in this sandbox (no Linux aarch64 build) — railway-query.sh uses direct GraphQL calls (Project-Access-Token header) as the documented fallback. ALSO FOUND AND FIXED (ADL-34, same PR): init-firewall.sh fail-open bug — one dead static domain (statsig.anthropic.com, NXDOMAIN) aborted the whole script before the default-DROP lockdown was ever applied, leaving the container's outbound network fully unrestricted every container start. Fixed by moving lockdown before domain resolution. FIRST REAL USE (same session) surfaced the actual root cause of the original stuck-deploy problem: the Railway project's plan is `trial`, and Railway was actively deprioritizing Trial/Hobby deploys platform-wide during a demand spike (2026-07-21, confirmed via Railway status/community reports) — not a code/config issue. Flagged to Ryan: confirm the Hobby-plan upgrade from ADL-32 actually completed; Pro tier is the only tier that fully bypasses the deploy queue. FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-21, ADL-34 §5): the container rebuild happened and surfaced a second bug in the same fix — GitHub itself failed the final verification (`unable to reach https://api.github.com`). Root cause: lockdown-before-resolution now blocks step 6's own `curl https://api.github.com/meta` bootstrap fetch (chicken-and-egg — GitHub's IPs aren't allowlisted yet because that fetch is what's supposed to allowlist them). Fixed by DNS-bootstrapping api.github.com's IP via `dig` (same pattern as the Turso/Railway entries) before the curl call. VERIFIED 2026-07-22: Ryan rebuilt the container since this fix; the following COO session made dozens of successful `gh` CLI calls throughout (gh pr create/merge, gh issue create/close, gh run list/view, across ~10 PRs) with zero firewall/DNS errors — direct end-to-end confirmation the GitHub-bootstrap fix holds post-rebuild. CLOSED — no further verification needed.

items.title: test-db.ts hand-mirrors 21 CREATE TABLE statements — silent schema-drift risk in every repository test
items.notes: Logged 2026-07-26 (COO) during the OP-15 prerequisite audit. Was previously untracked — it existed only as a sub-bullet inside OP-15's notes ('Q22 test-DDL consolidation'), so deferring OP-15 would have buried it. src/backend/repositories/__tests__/test-db.ts imports db/schema.ts for Drizzle typing but then hand-writes all 21 tables as literal DDL. A migration can therefore change the real schema while every repository test keeps passing green against the stale copy — the tests would not detect the drift. Same family as the stale local dev.db that caused a false alarm during the 2026-07-26 BUG-63 investigation (companions missing user_id post-migration 0012). Count has grown from the 13 recorded in OP-15's notes to 21, so this is actively worsening. Fix direction: drop the hand-written DDL and apply the real migrations to the in-memory libSQL DB (migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: 'src/backend/migrations' })) so the test schema is identical to production's by construction. IMPLEMENTATION CAVEAT for the brief: createTestDb() runs in beforeEach across ~580 backend tests, so replaying 12+ migration files per test may hurt suite time — build the schema once and clone per test rather than re-migrating. Also clears OP-15 prerequisite (a); sequence this BEFORE the OP-15 skills design pass. Scheduled as batch B9 in jobs/COO/backlog-clearance-plan.md.

items.title: UK constituent countries (Scotland etc.) unavailable when adding a place
items.notes: Found 2026-07-20 UAT. Countries are ISO 3166-1 (countryCode is the PK, e.g. 'US','AU') — Scotland/England/Wales/Northern Ireland aren't countries under that standard, they'd be Regions under GB, same tier as US states/AU provinces (GE-01/02/06). Fix: region_tier_enabled=1 + label 'Constituent Country', added England/Scotland/Wales/NI as regions (GB-ENG/SCT/WLS/NIR) via data-only custom migration, guarded to only patch already-seeded installs (self-caught a fresh-install idempotency bug in first draft — startup.service.ts seedRegions() would have been starved on a truly fresh install). items.title: Time-varying CI checks must not gate deploys — Dependency Vulnerability Scan excluded from the production branch
items.notes: ADL-40 (2026-07-26). Trigger: production deploys blocked outright — `Security Checks` failed on production@299ab5c (run 30210259329) on GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6 (body-parser, HIGH), and Railway gates prod deploys on CI green. Root cause is NOT the promotion: `npm audit` queries the advisory DB at run time, so the identical tree passed on main 2026-07-24 and failed on production 2026-07-26 (verified — `git diff 299ab5c 3889436 -- package-lock.json package.json` is empty; only drift-ledger/STATUS.md/tracker.json/park-doc changed between them). Deployability had become a function of the calendar. Fix: security.yml push trigger `branches: ["**"]` → `branches-ignore: ["production"]`; ci.yml deliberately unchanged and still gates prod. Does not weaken security — check runs attach to a commit SHA not a branch, and production is only ever fast-forwarded from main, so every promoted SHA already carries this workflow's green statuses; the re-run is skipped, the verdict is frozen at the point it was earned. Detection unchanged on PRs and main (how DEP-01/DEP-02 were both found). Residual accepted gap: a direct push to production bypassing main would be unscanned — contained by process (CLAUDE.md: production is ff-only, agents never touch it). Alternative of removing Railway's CI gate entirely rejected by PO. Deferred idea, not adopted: a scheduled nightly audit on main that opens an issue, which would also catch advisories landing against an unchanged main between PRs. Production promoted to ce5dbd5 same session, CI + Security Checks both green, deploy gate reopened. security-backlog.md bumped to v1.3 with a pointer section, same PR.

items.title: Staging Railway environment ALLOWED_ORIGINS missing https:// scheme — CORS blocks all asset requests, white screen
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21, immediately after OP-22 closed. PO reported staging white screen + empty Turso DB. Diagnosed via read-only diagnostics (turso-query.mjs + Railway deploymentLogs GraphQL query, both per the ADL-33 runbook): Turso staging DB is fine (own separate instance, fully migrated 12/12, 250 countries seeded) — 0 users because nobody's ever gotten past sign-in. Root cause confirmed directly from server logs: `[ERROR] GET /assets/index-BGMSZVwk.css 500 CORS: origin 'https://travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app' not allowed` (server.ts:122). Vite tags module scripts/stylesheets `crossorigin`, so the browser sends an Origin header on every asset request; CORS middleware does an exact string match against ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and the global error handler turns a rejection into a JSON 500 — browser sees wrong-MIME-type CSS + 500'd JS, i.e. white screen. EXACT ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by PO checking the Railway dashboard): Staging's ALLOWED_ORIGINS was set to the bare hostname `travel-tracker-staging.up.railway.app`, missing the `https://` scheme — `req.headers.origin` is always scheme-included, so the exact-match check in server.ts:119 never matched. FIXED 2026-07-21: PO added the `https://` scheme on the Railway dashboard and redeployed (deployment 12e1e764, 06:03 UTC). VERIFIED independently (not just PO's visual confirmation): new deployment's logs show zero CORS errors (vs. the prior deployment's immediate CORS rejection on every asset request); Turso staging `users` table now has 1 real row (`is_owner=0`, sign-in genuinely completed) — confirmed via turso-query.mjs, not just taking PO's word. CLOSED. Follow-on: this same verification pass surfaced BUG-60 (trust proxy / rate-limit misconfiguration, present in both prod and staging, unrelated to this fix).

items.title: Express 'trust proxy' not configured — express-rate-limit can't safely resolve client IPs behind Railway's proxy
items.notes: Found 2026-07-21 while verifying BUG-59's fix (deployment log review, both prod and staging). Railway sits its app behind a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For; server.ts never calls `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`, so Express defaults to not trusting it. express-rate-limit (SEC-07, server.ts ~L147-153) detects this mismatch and throws `ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR` (see https://express-rate-limit.github.io/ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR/). CONFIRMED PRESENT IN BOTH ENVIRONMENTS via deploymentLogs: staging deployment 12e1e764 (06:05 UTC) and prod deployment f60d623b (05:45 UTC, i.e. already present in prod BEFORE any of today's changes — this is not something today's session introduced). Severity assessment: fires once shortly after boot in both environments' logs, not repeated per-request — consistent with the app being otherwise functional (prod 'confirmed working' 2026-07-21 shakedown, staging sign-in completed successfully today), so this is NOT currently a hard block on traffic. The real concern is correctness/security of SEC-07's rate-limiting: without an explicit, correctly-scoped `trust proxy` value, IP attribution behind Railway's proxy may be inaccurate (all traffic bucketed under one apparent IP) or spoofable (a forged X-Forwarded-For header trusted when it shouldn't be) depending on how this actually resolves at runtime — needs an Architect read on the correct value (e.g. `trust proxy: 1` vs Railway's actual proxy count/CIDR) rather than a guessed one-liner, since getting this wrong in the other direction (trusting an untrusted hop) is its own security hole. Per the standing project rule that runtime/infrastructure config changes need Architect ADL before COO acts — not fixed unilaterally. Affects both environments identically; one fix branch covers both once specced. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-37 — `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` (hop-count integer, not `true`; `true` would trust the whole X-Forwarded-For chain and let a client forge/spoof req.ip to bypass the rate limit, which express-rate-limit itself rejects as ERR_ERL_PERMISSIVE_TRUST_PROXY). Implemented in server.ts + mirrored in server-test-app.ts; new regression test (trust-proxy.test.ts) asserts the compiled trust predicate accepts hop 0 and rejects hop 1, not just the literal setting value. GitHub issue #221 (closed via PR #222, squash-merged, CI 9/9 green). VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-22: Ryan approved promoting `main` → `production` (24 commits, incl. WP-01–04 Waypoint reskin + BUG-59) via the standard ADL-35 fast-forward; both envs redeployed (prod 8ca4c7fc, staging 4ff379e4) and their boot logs read clean via `railway-query.sh logs` — no ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR, no CORS errors, only an unrelated npm `production` config deprecation warning. CLOSED, both environments confirmed.

items.title: GET /api/admin/countries (and regions) require owner status — non-owner accounts can't populate the country picker on trip create
items.notes: Found 2026-07-22 live in staging (Ryan signed in as a non-owner test account). Map tab renders (base tiles need no API call) but with no shading and no legend key — GET /api/map/shading and GET /api/map/shading/config both 403 for non-owners, silently swallowed by the frontend. The actual blocker: TripForm.tsx's country picker (useAdmin.ts's useCountries, GET /api/admin/countries) renders empty, because that route is registered directly on adminRouter, which gates its ENTIRE router with requireOwner (admin.ts:27) — countries have no read/write split. Per GE-04/GE-05, every country ships as a global, pre-seeded default available to all users out of the box (same tier as AD-09's categories/activities, not owner-configured data) — so requireOwner on the GET path is wrong; only the admin-panel WRITE operations (PATCH country region-tier config, POST/PATCH regions) should stay owner-gated. Net effect: a non-owner account cannot get past country selection when creating a trip at all — full stop, this is the practical ceiling on 'share the app with a friend to test' raised this session. Related but distinct from BRD-AD07/BRD-AD08 (ADL-28, per-user map shading + companions, already tracked separately, 'awaiting Backend implementation brief') — those are about making owner-only data per-user; this is about global data incorrectly gated as owner-only. Scope for this bug: split admin.ts's countries/regions GET routes to requireAuth (any authenticated user can read), keep PATCH/POST under requireOwner. Routed to Architect first per this project's established pattern for auth-scoping changes (ADL-27/ADL-28 precedent) rather than a unilateral Backend patch. GitHub issue #225. RESOLVED 2026-07-22: ADL-38 — the two GET routes (countries, regions) moved above admin.ts's router-level requireOwner guard so they're requireAuth-only; all writes (PATCH country, POST/PATCH regions) stay owner-gated below the guard, fail-closed by default for any future route. ADL-27's file stamped SUPERSEDED IN PART per the document lifecycle rule. New regression coverage in security.access-matrix.test.ts Part E (non-owner GET → 200, non-owner write → 403). PR #227, CI 9/9 green, squash-merged. Manually verified with a non-owner bypass user: GET countries 200 (250 rows), GET regions 200, writes 403, other admin routes still 403 (fail-closed intact). CLOSED — non-owner trip creation works end-to-end, no frontend change needed.

Full detail in ADL-28's addendum and jobs/frontend/park-docs/20260723-FRONTEND-companions-api-route-park.txt. Not a security hole (backend correctly enforces per-user scoping either way) — pure UI-reachability gap. items.notes: Reported 2026-07-26 by Ryan: two independent live sightings on mobile, both non-owner accounts. Logged so this doesn't evaporate across a session boundary; Ryan is watching for a recurrence and will capture the actual network response next time. No brief until it's reproducible or a concrete lead surfaces.
